question: Does the RGB re-encoding quality advantage persist if all cancellation gates and variance updates follow the original latent receiver?
status_at_registration: The initial three-arm experiment had closed. RGB exceeded the native latent arm in weakest-user PSNR. This is a follow-up on the same observations.
new_arm: RGB re-encoding with all twelve native user/round gate tensors replayed. It also inherits the native residual variance schedule. Scoring truth remains outside the receiver.
reference: Unchanged formal native and free-gate RGB scores from the parent. Rerun only native demixing needed to expose unstored gate tensors. Check its final physical NMSE against the archived value for every quadruple.
statistics: Same 125 groups and original pairing. Average seeds within each quadruple. Reuse the 10000-draw common500 index bank of the parent. Pointwise 95% intervals.
budget: One shared A800, 30 minute wall limit. One new receiver arm on 750 existing four-user observations. No new images, channel draws, model fitting, hyperparameter selection or hardware latency estimate.
